_about: TRANSLATOR SHELF: Charles Wharton Stork (1881-1971): Modern Swedish Masterpieces (1923) and Söderberg's Martin Birck's Youth (Harper, 1930); Heidenstam's The Charles Men, Part I (American-Scandinavian Foundation, 1920), added in round 90. The Anthology of Swedish Lyrics (1917), also added in round 90, waits in _pending since round 103: its only scan is a library preservation photocopy. Round 117 (2026-10-17, vetoable) added Fröding's Selected Poems (Macmillan, 1916). Printings before 1931 only. US public domain. Added 2026-10-10 by lane C (round 33); Adam may veto. No uids minted.

cw-stork-soderberg-martin-birck-s-youth.note: Harper's first edition: 'Copyright 1930, by Harper & Brothers'. A 1930 US publication entered the US public domain on 1 January 2026.

cw-stork-heidenstam-charles-men-1.scan_edition: Scandinavian Classics XV, American-Scandinavian Foundation, New York 1920; archive.org scan
cw-stork-heidenstam-charles-men-1.note: Part II (Scandinavian Classics XVI) was not found as a scan.

cw-stork-froding-selected-poems.scan_edition: The Macmillan Company, New York; copyright 1916, published March 1916; UCLA scan

_pending.cw-stork-anthology-of-swedish-lyrics: Stork's Anthology of Swedish Lyrics (American-Scandinavian Foundation, 1917; IA scan): the only scan found (IA anthologyswedis00storgoog) is a library preservation photocopy on acid-free paper by Acme Bookbinding, Charlestown, Massachusetts (ANSI/NISO Z39.48-1992, so 1992 or later), so it waits on the facsimile ruling. Found in round 103; it had been shelved before.

_name_words_note: Translator name only: fetch_shelf.py treats it as the identity check, so the original author's name is deliberately NOT listed. 'stork' alone is left out as a common word.

cws-charles-men-1.post_1930_examined: Examined in round 90: 'DllU?,i 1965' is a garbled library stamp below the 1920 copyright line, not an imprint.

_verified_note: Evidence that each source's rights/identity line was read (lane C review fix, 2026-10-02, pipeline run over the fetched files; no book text recorded). PG: the header's Translator: line and the COPYRIGHTED marker. IA: whether the translator's name appears in the first 30 KB of OCR, and the years printed in the first 15 KB of front matter (scanner/digitizer lines skipped). Any post-1930 year there was examined by eye; see the title's scan_edition.
